stage1.impression: A clean, well-controlled studio packshot: the blue acrylic reads as tinted cast material with believable edge thickness and the horn's resin glows, but the whole frame is sterile and reads as a high-end render rather than a photograph. The speaker barely touches the paper (a faint grey line, no weight, no blue light thrown onto the floor), the horn carries hot plastic-looking streaks and a violet LED-like glow at its throat, and the pale top face dissolves into the backdrop.

blocking_9: The cabinet must sit on the paper: a visible contact shadow just under the plinth (lum_median <= 145 in the 35 px band below the cabinet, against about 173 on open floor) that fades over roughly 0.3-0.5 m
The tinted acrylic must throw its colour: a soft blue transmitted pool on the floor in front of or beside the cabinet, so the product lights its set
No clipped, streaky specular on the horn and no saturated violet glow at the throat that reads as an emitter
The cabinet's top face must separate from the backdrop (at least 30 levels darker than the wall behind it)
The paper should show a hint of tooth or tonal falloff rather than a perfectly smooth CG plane

defects.what: Contact shadow too weak: 160 directly under the cabinet against 174 on open floor; the speaker floats
No coloured light from the tinted acrylic on the floor; floor RGB is the same cool grey under and away from the cabinet
Clipped specular on the horn's upper-right rim (p95 225, 0.26% clipped)
Radial bright streaks inside the horn read as CG internal reflections, plastic rather than resin
Saturated violet-blue rim inside the throat (p95 183 on crushed black) reads as an LED, not light through resin
Top face median 215 against wall 232; the lid edge disappears into the backdrop
Floor is a perfectly smooth, untextured plane; reads as CG paper
Driver mass at throat 61% crushed with no shape (fixed by card; noted only)

changes.problem: The speaker does not sit on the paper: the floor wash fills the area under the cabinet and the contact shadow is almost invisible.

evidence.measured: lum_median 160.3 directly under the cabinet vs 173.6 on open floor at [250,2080,650,2150]; ratio 0.92

change.from: wash 0.5 W/m2; contact shadow strength 0.9, distance_m 0.32
change.to: wash 0.2 W/m2; contact shadow strength 1.0, distance_m 0.45 (core unchanged)

changes.expected: A soft grey shadow under and just in front of the plinth, darkest at the contact line and fading into the floor by about 0.4 m; open floor stays near its current level.

changes.problem: The tinted acrylic casts no colour on the set, so the speaker looks pasted on rather than lighting its surroundings.

evidence.measured: RGB median 156/167/174 under the cabinet vs 166/175/182 on open floor: same hue, no blue pool

change.to: add 'sweep' to receivers, el 32, so the back light passes through the cabinet and lands as a blue transmitted pool 0.1-0.4 m in front of the plinth

changes.expected: A soft, clearly blue (not grey) patch on the floor in front of the cabinet, saturation visibly above the surrounding floor.

changes.problem: The horn carries hot, streaky highlights that read as glossy plastic and clip on the upper-right rim.

evidence.measured: lum_p95 224.6, clip_pct 0.26; long radial streaks across the horn mouth

changes.expected: Rim highlight stays as a crisp line without clipping; interior streaks drop in contrast so the resin reads as a deep tinted solid.

changes.problem: A saturated violet rim at the throat reads like an LED inside the horn.

evidence.measured: lum_p95 183 and 1.07% clipped on a 30% crushed black ground

changes.expected: The throat edge keeps a thin dark-blue separation line but no glowing violet crescent.

changes.problem: The cabinet's top face is nearly as bright as the backdrop, so the top edge dissolves.
changes.expected: The top face reads as a mid-light tinted plane with a single crisp front-edge highlight, clearly darker than the wall.

changes.problem: The paper is a perfectly smooth plane with no tooth, which says CG.

evidence.measured: lum_range 11.5 including grain; no visible surface structure

change.to: same colour with a fine paper-tooth bump (scale about 0.5 mm, strength 0.05) and roughness 0.85

changes.expected: Floor shows a faint, non-repeating tooth at full size, no visible pattern.

changes.problem: Overall contrast is a touch flat in the floor and lower cabinet, keeping the image in render territory.

evidence.measured: lum_median 118.6, p5 21.4, p95 190.3; floor 160-175 almost uniform

changes.expected: Slightly more depth in the cabinet's lower half and the floor gradient without clipping the wall.

out_of_scope.request: Give the driver mass at the throat some readable shape (it is 61% crushed to black)
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes it as the resin's own depth; it is the product.

out_of_scope.request: The cloth disc and the white lining dominate the front and make the cabinet read as a cutaway
out_of_scope.why: Cover cloth and lining are the product's own materials.

out_of_scope.request: Interior radial streaks in the horn may partly come from the resin's internal geometry
out_of_scope.why: The horn shape and material are fixed; only the lighting change in c3 is in scope.
